subject: Janussi, Keeper of the Tome
fact: Janussi, Keeper of the Tome, was killed after eating dinner with his face intact and teeth whole; his heart was torn out, ribcage smashed, nose broken, tongue and fingertip blackened, and a chip found in his front tooth — all indicating he was alive during initial trauma and later desecrated post-mortem.
source_quote: He had been dead before his chest was opened.

subject: desecration of Janussi
fact: Janussi's body was meticulously desecrated after death — heart removed, ribcage shattered, nose broken prior to death, and black substance applied to finger and lip — suggesting a ritualistic or magical act performed with deliberate timing and calm intent.
source_quote: He had been desecrating a corpse at his leisure, with nowhere to be.

subject: unknown assailant
fact: The assailant exhibited extreme precision and calm, disabling Janussi before death (broken nose, chipped tooth) and then performing post-mortem desecration (heart removal, black substance application) — indicating familiarity with arcane practices and a desire to prevent resurrection or extract hidden knowledge.
source_quote: The blows had been precise. Too precise, too close together, for a man fighting back.

subject: black substance
fact: A mysterious black substance, darker than ink, was found on Janussi’s left forefinger, lower lip, and tongue — confirmed not to be ink or any known material, and resistant to identification even by Glabbagool, an ooze that has consumed the Underdark’s poisons and gloop.
source_quote: The skill wasn't in identifying the substance. It was in knowing, with certainty, what it was not.

subject: chip in front tooth
fact: A fresh, jagged chip in Janussi’s front tooth was found on the floor beside his body, indicating he fell face-first before death — a trauma unrelated to the post-mortem desecration but critical to establishing the timeline of events.
source_quote: He had fallen forward. Face-first. Chipped the tooth on the way down.

subject: Keeper's Chamber, Candlekeep
fact: The Keeper's Chamber was the site of Janussi’s murder and desecration — bloodless spray, scattered tooth fragment, smeared ink and black substance on clothing, and signs of a struggle or interruption during writing — all pointing to an attack occurring during or shortly after evening activities.
source_quote: Janussi had been taking notes when this happened. Writing hand, fresh stains.

subject: Candlekeep Librarians
fact: The Candlekeep Librarians, as keepers of arcane texts, were likely targets of the attack — Janussi was actively writing in the books at time of death, suggesting the assailant sought to silence or intercept knowledge contained in his notes.
source_quote: Wasn't the blue ink — the ink they used in the books? It was.

subject: origin of the black substance
fact: The black substance on Janussi’s body resists identification even by Glabbagool — implying it is either an unknown poison, a magical residue, or a substance native to a realm beyond the Underdark — and its presence on the lip and finger suggests it was ingested or applied as part of a ritual or curse.
source_quote: When even a creature that has eaten the Underdark can't place a poison, you've learned the poison is worth being afraid of.

subject: timing of the nose fracture
fact: The broken nose occurred before death, as bruising requires living tissue — placing the initial assault within the narrow window between Janussi’s last meal and his death, and suggesting the attacker was present during a private moment.
source_quote: Bruising doesn't form on a corpse; there's no living tissue to swell.

subject: purpose of the finger-to-lip gesture
fact: The pattern of black substance on finger and lip mirrors the habitual gesture of a reader wetting their fingertip to turn pages — implying the victim was reading or writing when attacked, and the assailant may have used this gesture to apply the poison as part of a cursed text or sentient ink.
source_quote: Turning pages, wetting the fingertip the way readers do without thinking, a hundred times an hour, never once considering that the page might be the thing reading them.
